summary.headline: Happy Forgings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32.7% YoY to Rs.501 crore and PAT grew 32.8% to Rs.98 crore; Rs.500 crore new capex approved.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached Rs.501 crore (+32.7% YoY) on 24.8% volume growth and 6.3% higher realisations to Rs.267/kg. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs.950 crore (+29.9%), with PAT up 35.8% to Rs.189 crore and PAT margin of 19.9%. Management approved an additional Rs.500 crore capex, mainly machining, phased across FY28-FY29, on top of the Rs.650 crore heavy-component programme that is now guided to commission in Q4 FY28. Management reiterated that full-year margins may be similar to FY26, citing raw material pass-through and higher export freight costs.

financial_highlights.metric: Finished goods volume growth Q2 FY27

financial_highlights.change: Hit by receivables build-up and Rs.35 crore advances to raw material suppliers

financial_highlights.value: ROE 17.1%, ROCE 19.6%; ROCE on operational assets above 25%

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / TOL to TNW

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: 33% of H1 FY27 revenue (37% in H1 FY26); high-teens growth with domestic up mid-20s, while exports were subdued by longer shipment times and higher sales in transit.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 30% of H1 FY27 revenue (34% in H1 FY26); growth over 20%, domestic high-teens. Domestic market share rose from 42% to nearly 46%.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: 16% of H1 FY27 revenue (13% in H1 FY26); growth well above 50% in both domestic and export markets.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 12% of H1 FY27 revenue (10% in H1 FY26); growth over 50% across domestic and export.

segments.name: Passenger vehicle
segments.commentary: 9% of H1 FY27 revenue (5% in H1 FY26); revenue almost doubled YoY, with new North American PV line ramping and sales largely in transit.

guidance_outlook: Management is well positioned to meet full-year volume growth guidance, supported by order book and ramp-up of recently secured business.
Full-year profitability margins may remain roughly similar to FY2026 levels, with near-term pressure from raw material prices and shipment costs.
Gross margin and EBITDA per kg are expected to keep trending upward through favourable mix, value addition and efficiencies.
Heavy-component facility (Rs.650 crore capex, with 20 MW captive solar) to commission in Q4 FY28; revenue assumed only from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Around Rs.500 crore of data-centre-related orders targeted by March 2027; cold trials Jan-Feb 2027, hot trials by March 2027.
Solar plant to add about 1.5% to EBITDA; around Rs.30 crore of power savings; full generation from Q1 FY28.
Total capacity to reach about 2,17,000 t forging and 1,16,000 t machining in two to two and a half years.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity: forging 1,58,000 t and machining 82,000 t. H1 FY27 utilisation was 60% in forging and 77% in machining; machining expected to reach about 90% by Q4.

Rs.650 crore heavy-component capex: Rs.300 crore already invested; around Rs.50 crore in FY27 and balance in FY28. Includes about Rs.300 crore hammer line (fungible, 300 kg to 3 t), Rs.200-250 crore dedicated machining lines, and Rs.150 crore vertical upsetter line for wind and North American farm equipment.

New Rs.500 crore capex approved by board, 70% machining and 30% small press forging lines, funded by debt and internal accruals, phased over FY28-FY29. Land already acquired. Planned Rs.300 crore bank debt, possibly as bridge loan and need-based.
Planned additions of 59,000 t forging and 34,000 t machining capacity. Forging press commissioned in Q1 FY27 and additional hammer in Q2 FY27.
Hammer line capacity about 2,000 t per month; management cites about 1.3x asset turn, with a potential Rs.1,600-1,800 crore annual opportunity if sold as machined product.
demand_pricing: Export order book is roughly 50% of total; about Rs.95 crore of orders won in Q2 for Asia exports. Total MHCV order book cited as Rs.950 crore, plus about Rs.500 crore gained in the last quarter.

Realisations rose on raw material pass-through, negotiated price increases for conversion costs and favourable mix. About 80% of cost increases passed through; about 80% of domestic OEMs have paid the increases. Export ocean freight costs roughly doubled in Q2, not yet fully recovered.
Data-centre business: about Rs.300 crore of orders secured, with visibility to 2033, and about Rs.1,000 crore of new orders under discussion; management aims to close about Rs.500 crore by FY27-end.
Farm equipment: about 4-5% of the 30% segment is indirect exports; management reports no order-book impact from OEM caution, though November-December looked weaker.
A recently added domestic CV customer's acquisition of a European CV company may bring supply-chain opportunities; RFQs have started, with business expected in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book and pipeline is export-linked, and how is the new Rs.500 crore capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 50% of the order book is export, with over Rs.95 crore of recent Asia export orders. The Rs.500 crore capex is 70% machining and 30% small press forging lines, with land already acquired.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 4,000-ton press line built for a North American PV customer, and what revenue will it generate?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it serves a North American PV client and ramped up in Q1-Q2. Sales are largely DAP and in transit, recognised from Q3. Management projects about Rs.80-100 crore of sales from this facility.

qa_highlights.question: Has the heavy-line commissioning timeline changed from Q4 to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No change: equipment arrived in FY27, full forging trials are planned for Q4 FY27, and sample submissions and revenue begin in FY28 Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any risk to data-centre capex given US election concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no issue: the customer has already invested, the market is short of heavy-forging capacity, and even Rs.1,000 crore of orders is about 5% of the total market.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins moderate to FY26 levels given strong H1, and is it due to pass-through or cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA per kg has improved despite cost pressures and should be maintained in H2. Raw materials are fully passed through; the solar plant adds about 1.5% to EBITDA from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt will fund the new Rs.500 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management proposes Rs.300 crore of bank debt as a bridge, need-based and possibly partly utilised, with the rest from internal accruals and cash over 1.5-2 years.

risks_watch: Data-centre order conversion: about Rs.500 crore targeted by March 2027 versus Rs.300 crore secured; cold and hot trials are on a tight schedule.
Margin trajectory: management guided full-year margins similar to FY26 despite H1 expansion, with freight and raw material pressure.
Export shipment timing: DAP-basis sales in transit, with North American PV revenue recognised from Q3.
Heavy-component facility timing: commissioning in Q4 FY28, with revenues only from Q3-Q4 FY28.
Working capital: H1 operating cash flow was Rs.124 crore against EBITDA of Rs.294 crore, due to receivables and advances.
Promoter stake dilution pending under SEBI norms, per an analyst question; management says it will comply within the timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, capacity and new orders, with specific timelines. Somewhat evasive on the margin guidance and on the split between dedicated and fungible capex, and it answered some questions by reframing them.
key_quotes: Raw material prices are a complete pass-through for us.
The absolute EBITDA per kg, despite the cost pressures, have improved, if you see, which is an important point to be seen.
Rs.300 crores is the optimum sanction, you can say, but maybe actual utilization can be lower in the area.
Out of the Rs.650 crores capex, Rs.150 crores is towards wind and North American tractor products, which is altogether a different line.

adds.what: Heavy-component facility (Rs.650 crore capex incl. hammer line, machining lines, vertical upsetter; 20 MW captive solar)
New Rs.500 crore board-approved capex: 70% machining, 30% small press forging lines, phased FY28-FY29
Planned additions of 59,000 t forging and 34,000 t machining capacity (total to ~2,17,000 t forging, ~1,16,000 t machining in 2-2.5 years)

growth.why: Management says it is well positioned to meet FY27 volume growth guidance (order book, ramp-up), but full-year margins are guided only roughly similar to FY26 (a cut from trend), with forging utilisation at 60%, and new Rs.500 cr capex phased FY28-29 plus Rs.650 cr heavy-component facility commissioning Q4 FY28; Rs.300 cr data-centre orders secured with ~Rs.500 cr targeted by FY27-end.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided full-year FY27 profitability margins roughly similar to FY26, despite H1 EBITDA margin of 30.9% (+127 bps), citing raw material prices and export freight costs that roughly doubled in Q2 and are not yet fully recovered.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Forging press commissioned Q1 FY27 and additional hammer Q2 FY27; heavy-component facility (Rs.650 cr, Rs.300 cr already invested) guided to commission Q4 FY28, with 59,000 t forging and 34,000 t machining additions planned in 2-2.5 years, though forging utilisation is only 60%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 FY27 finished-goods volume grew 24.8% YoY and management says it is well positioned to meet FY27 volume growth guidance on order book (Rs.950 cr MHCV order book plus about Rs.500 cr added last quarter).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved an additional Rs.500 cr capex (70% machining, 30% small press forging) phased FY28-FY29 with land already acquired; machining utilisation at 77% heading to about 90% by Q4 also supports further capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Full-year margin guidance was cut to roughly FY26 levels despite H1 PAT margin of 19.9% (+86 bps), and volume guidance was only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight costs roughly doubled in Q2 and are not fully recovered, and Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs.501 cr sits on Rs.267/kg realisation; November-December farm equipment demand looked weaker and data-centre orders need to convert from Rs.300 cr secured to about Rs.500 cr by March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Data-centre heavy forgings need cold trials Jan-Feb 2027 and hot trials by March 2027 (about Rs.300 cr secured, about Rs.500 cr targeted by FY27-end); heavy-component facility commissions Q4 FY28 with revenue from Q3-Q4 FY28.

rows.label: Data-centre orders to Rs.500 cr by FY27-end
rows.why: About Rs.300 cr secured with visibility to 2033 and about Rs.1,000 cr under discussion; management aims to close about Rs.500 cr by FY27-end, with cold trials Jan-Feb 2027.

rows.label: Solar plant EBITDA and power savings
rows.why: The 20 MW captive solar plant adds about 1.5% to EBITDA and about Rs.30 cr of power savings, with full generation from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Working capital unwind
rows.why: H1 FY27 operating cash flow was only Rs.124 cr against EBITDA of Rs.294 cr, due to receivables build-up and Rs.35 cr advances to raw material suppliers, with DAP-basis export sales still in transit.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the data-centre pipeline, and capacity timelines, but cautious and somewhat evasive on full-year margin guidance and the split between dedicated and fungible capex; analysts pressed on margins, debt funding and the data-centre orders.
